pendingTriage.draft:
Hi Peter,

Thanks for the kind words — glad SpotOn has been working well for you overall!

That's an interesting bug report. To be transparent: I'm not immediately certain what's causing "Don't Stop The Music" to revert to "SpotOn Recommendations" — this isn't something I've seen reported before, so I want to make sure I understand it correctly before suggesting a fix.

A couple of questions to help narrow it down:

[B]1.[/B] When does the revert happen? Is it immediately after you change it, after a player reconnect, or after an LMS restart?

[B]2.[/B] Does it affect all your players, or just specific ones?

[B]3.[/B] Which version of SpotOn and LMS are you running? You can find both in [B]Settings → Manage Plugins → SpotOn[/B].

In the meantime, it would be really helpful if you could grab a diagnostic bundle — go to [B]Settings → Manage Plugins → SpotOn → Diagnostics[/B] and download the bundle. This will give me context on how SpotOn is registering itself with LMS's DSTM framework.

My initial suspicion is that SpotOn is registering as a DSTM provider and something in that registration is inadvertently overriding your player preference — but I don't want to guess without more data.

Could you please open a GitHub issue for this so it doesn't get lost in the forum thread? You can do that here:

[URL]https://github.com/stiefenm/spoton/issues[/URL]

Include the diagnostic bundle and answers to the questions above if possible. That way I can track it properly and push a fix if it turns out to be a genuine bug.

Thanks for taking the time to report it — these subtle integration issues are easy to miss!

pendingTriage.draft:
[QUOTE=CJS]I suppose that this behavior is related to the "Autoplay" setting under SpotOn player settings. I suspect that when you disable SpotOn AutoPlay for all your players, the behavior will go back to normal.[/QUOTE]

That's a great spot, CJS — and very likely correct!

[B]fanshawe[/B], the [B]Autoplay[/B] setting in SpotOn's per-player settings controls whether SpotOn registers itself as a "Don't Stop The Music" provider. When it's enabled, LMS picks it up as an available recommendation source, and depending on your LMS version, it can override your preferred DSTM setting.

To fix this, try the following:

[B]1.[/B] Go to [B]Settings → Player → SpotOn[/B] for each of your players
[B]2.[/B] Find the [B]Autoplay[/B] option and set it to [B]Disabled[/B]
[B]3.[/B] Restart LMS and check if the DSTM setting now holds

You'll need to do this for [B]each player individually[/B] — the setting is per-player, not global.

If disabling Autoplay resolves it, that confirms the cause. If the DSTM setting still reverts to "SpotOn Recommendations" even after disabling Autoplay on all players, that would point to a bug worth investigating further.

In that case, please do the following:
[LIST]
[*]Grab a diagnostic bundle from [B]SpotOn Settings → Diagnostics[/B]
[*]Open a bug report at [URL]https://github.com/stiefenm/spoton/issues[/URL] with the details
[/LIST]

Thanks for the report — this is useful feedback regardless, as the interaction between SpotOn's Autoplay feature and the DSTM setting probably deserves clearer documentation or at minimum a warning in the UI.

Glad that sorted it out, Peter!

You raise a fair point about the UX — it's not obvious that SpotOn's [B]Autoplay[/B] setting effectively takes over the "Don't Stop The Music" option in the main player settings. Ideally, SpotOn should either respect the top-level setting or make the relationship between the two much clearer to the user.

I've noted this as a usability improvement worth addressing. If you'd like to see it tracked formally, feel free to open a GitHub Issue so it doesn't get lost:

[URL]https://github.com/stiefenm/spoton/issues[/URL]

Thanks for the feedback — it genuinely helps make the plugin better for everyone!
